verses.pali: Atha kho somā bhikkhunī pubbaṇhasamayaṁ nivāsetvā pattacīvaramādāya sāvatthiṁ piṇḍāya pāvisi.
verses.english: Then the nun Somā robed up in the morning and, taking her bowl and robe, entered Sāvatthī for alms.

verses.pali: Sāvatthiyaṁ piṇḍāya caritvā pacchābhattaṁ piṇḍapātapaṭikkantā yena andhavanaṁ tenupasaṅkami divāvihārāya.
verses.english: She wandered for alms in Sāvatthī. After the meal, on her return from almsround, she went to the Dark Forest for the day’s meditation,

verses.pali: Andhavanaṁ ajjhogāhetvā aññatarasmiṁ rukkhamūle divāvihāraṁ nisīdi.
verses.english: plunged deep into it, and sat at the root of a tree to meditate.

verses.pali: Atha kho māro pāpimā somāya bhikkhuniyā bhayaṁ chambhitattaṁ lomahaṁsaṁ uppādetukāmo samādhimhā cāvetukāmo yena somā bhikkhunī tenupasaṅkami; upasaṅkamitvā somaṁ bhikkhuniṁ gāthāya ajjhabhāsi:
verses.english: Then Māra the Wicked, wanting to make the nun Somā feel fear, terror, and goosebumps, wanting to make her fall away from immersion, went up to her and addressed her in verse:
it’s for the sages to attain.
it’s not possible for a woman.”

verses.pali: “ko nu khvāyaṁ manusso vā amanusso vā gāthaṁ bhāsatī”ti?
verses.english: “Who’s speaking this verse, a human or a non-human?”

verses.pali: “māro kho ayaṁ pāpimā mama bhayaṁ chambhitattaṁ lomahaṁsaṁ uppādetukāmo samādhimhā cāvetukāmo gāthaṁ bhāsatī”ti.
verses.english: “This is Māra the Wicked, wanting to make me feel fear, terror, and goosebumps, wanting to make me fall away from immersion!”

verses.pali: Atha kho somā bhikkhunī “māro ayaṁ pāpimā” iti viditvā māraṁ pāpimantaṁ gāthāhi paccabhāsi:
verses.english: Then Somā, knowing that this was Māra the Wicked, replied to him in verse:
as you rightly discern the Dhamma.
is fit for Māra to address.”

verses.pali: Atha kho māro pāpimā “jānāti maṁ somā bhikkhunī”ti dukkhī dummano tatthevantaradhāyīti.
verses.english: Then Māra the Wicked, thinking, “The nun Somā knows me!” miserable and sad, vanished right there.
